rationale: Case shortlisted by existing M1 research candidate protocol, not optimized against a G1 result. Official runc release and dated Snyk early report plus independent Red Hat 2019 background and Palo Alto later analysis offer a plausible chronology. Actual version availability, novel later labels and experiment suitability remain unreviewed.
population_caveat: CVE-2024-21626 is a disclosed vulnerability and potential container escape, not verified evidence that a real-world intrusion or observed runtime attack occurred.

git_provenance_anchor.warning: The official tag-reference API URL is a discovery pointer, not a frozen Git object or SHA-256 of archived report bytes. Resolve original tag and commit identities separately and independently audit the actual approved bytes. Tagger timestamps before embargo do not establish public availability.

sources.revision_risk: Publisher's current linked coverage and overview have later revisions (overview last updated 2025-05-27); cannot treat today's HTML as original.

notes_on_selection: Cutoff at midnight 2024-02-01 UTC is a PROPOSAL only, chosen to be after public January 31 disclosures and before the February 5 Palo Alto article, not a verified time for a frozen source revision.

Upstream runc maintainers and Snyk Research are distinct publishers but co-disclosure teams may share underlying findings; screen source-level factual independence rather than assume statistical independence.
An independent Feb 5 article does not automatically provide a novel fact. Reject this case if held-out facts are merely repeated early facts or cannot be judged without post-cutoff knowledge.
Later Snyk deep dive must never be a separate independent gold source when Snyk is included in the early report group.
Never infer that a CVE disclosure is a successful incident, observed compromise or deployed attack telemetry.
